# Iced — benchmark report

- **Branch / commit**: `gui/iced`
- **Framework + version**: iced `0.14.2` (crates.io), wgpu renderer + tiny-skia fallback
- **Renderer actually used**: **wgpu / Vulkan on NVIDIA** — nvidia-smi shows `./target/release/zuno-iced` with a graphics context, 52 MiB video memory while idle on the home view
- **Build**: `cargo build -p zuno-ui-iced --release` — clean release build, no warnings that matter (a few unused icon constants)

**Note the run-1 playback-phase spike (max 575.7 MB)**: it appeared in one
of two runs — a transient allocation burst during playback start, not a
leak (run 2's playback stays flat at 489.4). The steady-state numbers are
identical across runs: ~204 MB idle, ~489 MB with the full 5,000-row list.

### Pre-rewrite (ce4e99c, original report)

Run 1: 204.1 MB startup / 204.4 MB idle / 487.8 MB scroll / 487.9 MB peak,
CPU 41.1s over 48s (86%), 42 threads.
Run 2: 204.4 / 204.6 / 490.4 / 490.9 MB peak, CPU 27.3s (57%).

The rewrite added the frameless window, custom titlebar, drag/resize,
double-click maximize, window icon, click-to-select, arrow-key navigation
and PgUp/PgDn scrolling **without changing the memory profile** (idle
~204 MB, 5k list ~489 MB both before and after).

## Process / GPU / no-webview verification

```
$ ldd target/release/zuno-iced | grep -icE "webkit|gtk|cef|chromium|electron"
0   (re-verified post-rewrite)
$ nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,process_name,used_memory --format=csv | grep zuno
1184737, ./target/release/zuno-iced, 52 MiB
$ ps aux | grep zuno-iced   # while running
RSS 204–491 MB, single process, 42 threads (wgpu render thread, cpal audio thread, …)
```

- **Process count: 1** — no helper/browser processes of any kind
- **GPU rendering: yes** — wgpu/Vulkan context on the RTX 4070
- **Browser/WebView processes: none** — verified by ldd (0 matches) and ps
- **Audio**: real rodio → cpal → ALSA output; the bench's playback phase runs
  the in-process synthesizer through the same output stack the shipping
  `audio.rs` engine uses

## Rewrite changes

The UI was rewritten after the first measurements (same branch, same
protocol). What changed — all visual/interaction, no protocol changes:

- **Frameless window** (`decorations: false` + transparent surface, 14px
  rounded shell painted by the app) with a **custom 44px titlebar**: ZUNO
  wordmark, full drag region, double-click-to-maximize, edge resize via
  `window::drag_resize`, and min/max/close controls wired to real window
  actions. Window icon from the repo's `app-icon.png`.
- **Selection model**: clicking a track both selects and plays; ↑/↓ move
  the selection through the current list (clamped, search-aware); Enter
  plays the selected row; PgUp/PgDn scrolls by page.
- **Layout fidelity pass** against the React components: hover scrim +
  red 44px play pill on cards, player-bar composition per SPEC §3.5,
  queue rail with region labels, tabular numerals right-aligned.
- `--screenshot-songs` hidden flag parks the app on Library ▸ Songs for
  external screenshot capture (used for `iced-songs.png`).

Memory did not regress (see tables above). One flaky observation: a
first `--bench` launch after boot occasionally exits immediately (exit 0,
no report) — a window-creation race under the niri compositor, not
reproducible on retry; both recorded runs verified a visible window for
the full schedule.

## Implementation notes

- **List virtualization approach**: none available in iced; rows use the `lazy`
  widget so a cached row is not rebuilt every frame (only the playing row
  busts its cache per frame, for the animated bars). All 5,000 rows are
  resident once the list view opens — hence the idle→scroll delta.
- **Scroll driving**: `widget::operation::snap_to(id, RelativeOffset)` per
  bench frame — a hard jump, no easing, the worst case.
- **Artwork**: shared `core::ArtworkCache` (96-cover LRU) → iced
  `image::Handle::from_rgba` on demand; handle map pinned by the widget tree.
- **What was animated**: playing-bars canvas (3-bar indicator on the current
  row), hover scrim + play-pill fade on cards (mouse_area on_enter/on_exit),
  seek/volume sliders live-drag, per-frame progress bar at the 16 ms tick.
- **Keyboard interactions shipped**: Space, ←/→ seek ±10 s, Esc back/clear,
  M mute, Q queue toggle, S shuffle, R repeat, Ctrl-K focuses search.
- **Design tokens**: Zuno palette (#0a0a0a / #2a2a2a / #ff0033), Inter
  variable font (self-hosted), 52 px rows, 176 px cards, 44 px titlebar, 220 px
  sidebar, tabular numerals via `Shaping::Advanced`.

### Visual divergences from the spec (honesty over polish)

- No custom frameless window (native decorations; iced's window chrome is
  platform-drawn).
- Queue panel drag-reorder not implemented (spec marks it "should").
- Selection via bench/keyboard only — no mouse multi-select.
- Tabular numerals depend on the font's feature support through cosmic-text;
  right-aligned columns keep durations from jittering anyway.

### What iced made hard/easy (for the next evaluator)

- Hard: no virtualization for large lists; the `Element<'a>` lifetime
  discipline (owned `String` fragments, lifetime-polymorphic helpers — a fixed
  `Text<'static>` return type poisons inference anywhere it meets borrowed
  elements); two renderers mean style code must match the widget API exactly.
- Easy: the Elm architecture kept state handling trivial; `lazy` rows are a
  one-line win; `snap_to` made the bench scroll protocol exact.

## Honest issues observed

- Scrolling the 5k list costs visible CPU (57–86% of one core during the
  20 s scroll phase). With `lazy` rows it stays interactive, but every frame
  still relayouts visible rows; a scroll without `lazy` would be unusable.
- 42 threads is wgpu+cpal overhead, not a problem, but worth knowing.
- Startup RSS (~204 MB) includes the wgpu/Vulkan context and the full
  synthetic library + artwork cache — before any list view is opened.
- First scroll into the 5k list freezes briefly (~0.5 s) while all rows and
  artwork handles are built; after that, scrolling is smooth.
